q7.answer: Every API and inference instance polls the serving config record every 10 seconds. When its `revision` changes, the instance applies the new snapshot. Inference instances load any version they don't already hold, check its checksum and warm it up, then switch to the new `active_version` atomically. No redeploy is needed, because the version is read from config and not built into the deployment.

q8.answer: The API puts a small event (request_id, user_id, the active output and so on) into a bounded in-memory buffer without blocking, after the user's response is written. A background thread then publishes it to the shadow queue. The shadow worker does its own online feature lookup for the candidate's feature groups, on a separate rate-limited client. So shadow never runs on the request thread and cannot add to the user's latency.

q9.answer: Work is dropped, not delayed. A full API buffer or an unreachable queue drops the event and counts it as `shadow_dropped`. Queue messages older than 5 minutes are skipped as stale rather than drained late, because late runs would see different features. A circuit breaker also pauses shadow when the user-path feature lookup slows down. Any day with more than 5% of events dropped is marked not_counted toward the 7 days.

q10.answer: Active output goes to the response log and candidate output goes to the shadow log, both in the warehouse. A daily job joins them on `request_id` and writes one row per version per day to a shadow metrics table. Gate metrics are error rate and p99 inference latency. Comparison-only metrics include overlap@20, rank correlation, catalog coverage and category spread, plus coverage and data-quality figures.

q11.answer: There are two guards. First, any config change that sets a version as shadow, preload or active is rejected unless every feature group it needs is online in the feature catalog, with a matching schema version and a successful materialization within 6 hours. Second, every request checks freshness and completeness: the API in step 3 and the shadow worker in step 15. If a group is missing or stale, the model is never called, and the shadow worker records `skipped_missing_features`. The catalog also blocks removing a group that the active, previous or shadow version needs.

q12.answer: A rollback, started by an automatic trigger or by on-call running `rollback`, is one compare-and-set that swaps `active_version` with `previous_version` and writes the change history. The previous version is kept loaded and warmed up on every inference instance, so it only needs a pointer swap on the next 10-second poll. Instances that haven't caught up after 60 seconds raise an alert and are taken out of the load balancer. The 1-minute guarantee covers only rolling back to `previous_version` while the config store is reachable.
